qt: to the Commission Fabio De Masi (NI) Subject:

News outlet Euractiv has reported the following on the limited access to the 13rd floor of the Commission’s Berlaymont building in Brussels: ‘Access to the 13th floor of the Berlaymont, where Ursula von der Leyen lives and her close circle works, will be severely limited from now on – even for Commissioners and senior officials – according to an internal memo seen by Euractiv. The top brass must now access their “conviviality salons” via the “purple elevators”, whatever that means [...]’1 1.
Is Euractiv’s reporting on the limited access to Ursula von der Leyen by Commissioners and senior officials correct?
What purpose do the Berlaymont’s ‘purple elevators’ serve in this context?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.1.2026) The Commission does not comment on the specifics of its security measures and installations. Its security policies and procedures are designed to ensure the highest level of protection for the Commission’s staff, visitors, and assets, and they are regularly reviewed and updated to reflect the evolving security landscape and to address identified risks.
